desktopPage.guide.title: Install 6529 Desktop
desktopPage.guide.lead: From the download to signing in, on Windows or a Mac, with what to check at each step.
desktopPage.guide.windows:
## Install on Windows

1. Open {setup}. It installs 6529 Desktop for your Windows user only, so it does not ask for an administrator password.
2. If Windows shows a warning about the file, check that it names the publisher **{publisher}** before you go on.
3. When it finishes, open 6529 Desktop from the Start menu.
desktopPage.guide.mac:
## Install on a Mac

1. Open {dmg} and move 6529 Desktop into your Applications folder.
2. Open 6529 Desktop from Applications. The first time, macOS asks whether to open an app you downloaded from the internet: choose **Open**. The app is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple.
3. 6529.io opens in the app's own window.
desktopPage.guide.signIn:
## Sign in

6529 Desktop cannot use browser extensions directly. Choose **Connect wallet**, then one of the two ways in:

- **Scan with a phone wallet**: WalletConnect. Scan the QR code with the wallet app on your phone.
- **Use a browser wallet**: MetaMask, Rabby and other browser extensions. The app opens a page in your web browser. Connect your wallet there and sign the sign-in message, which costs nothing, then return to 6529 Desktop. The app waits two minutes.

Your session is kept in your operating system's credential store, and the long-lived session token is never given to the page.
desktopPage.guide.browserSigning:
## Sign with a browser wallet

If you signed in with a browser wallet, the wallet is not inside the app. When 6529 Desktop needs a signature, for example to post a drop or to vote in a decision, it opens a page in your web browser that shows what you are asked to sign.

1. The app shows a **request code** and a **content fingerprint**. The browser page shows the same two. Check that they match. The fingerprint is a short code made from the exact content you are asked to sign, so a different request shows a different fingerprint. If either one differs, do not sign: choose **Cancel** in the app and close the browser page.
2. Read what the page says you are signing, then sign in your wallet, or decline.
3. Return to 6529 Desktop. It checks the signature before it uses it. If you change your mind, choose **Cancel** in the app; the request also ends by itself after two minutes.

6529 never asks for your recovery phrase or password. Signing costs nothing and sends no transaction. Transactions, such as minting, delegation and market trades, are not sent to your browser wallet from the app: continue on 6529.io in your browser.
desktopPage.guide.update:
## Update

Later releases install updates themselves: the notice offers **Download update**, shows the progress, then **Restart to update**, and offers **Try again** if a download fails. Only an app that cannot install updates itself (or cannot tell whether it can) offers **Open download page** instead, which opens the download page in your browser. You can always download a release by hand from the [download page](https://6529.io/desktop).

0.1.0-rc.2 runs the copy of 6529.io that was built into it, with the old update notice. When a newer version is published, that notice shows a **Download** button that does not work, and nothing published on 6529.io changes that for 0.1.0-rc.2. If you use 0.1.0-rc.2, open [https://6529.io/desktop](https://6529.io/desktop) in your browser and download the next version by hand, once. Check its SHA-256 and install it the way you installed the first one.
desktopPage.guide.uninstall:
## Uninstall

- **Windows**: in Settings, open Apps, find 6529 Desktop and choose **Uninstall**. The uninstaller keeps your app data unless you choose to delete it.
- **Mac**: quit 6529 Desktop, then move it from your Applications folder to the Trash.

desktopPage.knownIssues.body:
## Installing

### 1. The Windows uninstaller is not signed yet

The installer and the programs it installs are signed by {publisher}. The uninstaller that it writes on your computer is not.

### 2. 6529 Desktop takes over `core6529://` links

Installing 6529 Desktop makes `core6529://` links open 6529 Desktop instead of the older 6529 Core app. On Windows, uninstalling 6529 Desktop removes that link registration.

## Using the app

### 3. Transactions continue in your browser

With a profile that signed in with a browser wallet, transactions such as minting, delegation and market trades are not sent to your wallet from the app. Continue them on 6529.io in your browser.

### 4. 0.1.0-rc.2 cannot update itself

0.1.0-rc.2 runs the copy of 6529.io that was built into it, with the old update notice. When a newer version is published, that notice shows a **Download** button that does not work, and nothing published on 6529.io changes that for 0.1.0-rc.2. If you use 0.1.0-rc.2, open [https://6529.io/desktop](https://6529.io/desktop) in your browser and download the next version by hand, once. Later releases install updates themselves: the notice offers **Download update**, shows the progress, then **Restart to update**, and offers **Try again** if a download fails. Only an app that cannot install updates itself (or cannot tell whether it can) offers **Open download page** instead, which opens the download page in your browser. You can always download a release by hand from the [download page](https://6529.io/desktop).

## Systems

### 5. No Linux version yet

There is no Linux version yet. It comes later.

### 6. Macs with Apple silicon only

The Mac app runs on Macs with Apple silicon (M1 or later) only.

desktopPage.guide.before:
## Before you start

- **A computer it runs on**: Windows (64-bit, Intel or AMD), or a Mac with Apple silicon. There is no Linux version yet.
- **A wallet to sign in with**: a wallet app on your phone that supports WalletConnect, or a wallet extension in your web browser, such as MetaMask or Rabby.
- **The installer for your system**, from the [download page](/desktop). Check its SHA-256 there before you open it.
